page: Microsoft Azure EC64as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, designed for resource-demanding workloads requiring substantial system memory and dedicated computing capacity. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, the instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by standard hardware cryptographic extensions including AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory-to-compute ratio. This high memory density aligns with memory-bound applications. The configuration does not include local disk storage, operating instead with network-attached Premium Storage capabilities. Acceleration hardware is not present, as the instance features zero GPUs. Public network connectivity requires configuration, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate distinct parallel processing strength. In multi-core compute tests via stress-ng, the EC64as_v5 achieved a score of 74,075.89, placing it in the top 25 percent tier, while its single-core compute performance registered at an average 2,330.07. In in-memory data processing, the instance recorded strong throughput with Redis SET operations reaching 62.05 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the EC64as_v5 presents strong resource density for organizations running heavy parallel tasks requiring low per-gigabyte overhead. Because it lacks bundled local disks, users rely on external block storage, which isolates data persistence costs. The server is well suited for in-memory databases like Redis, extensive caching tiers, large-scale relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise-resource-planning (ERP) deployments.
